correctness.rationale: For each labelled tuple poset Q, an assignment of one-point insertion patterns is globally compatible exactly when the unions of base-below and base-above tuple vertices do not overlap. Checking both directions of transitivity proves this finite-extension bijection. Orientation templates cover precisely the compatible assignments, and finite inclusion-exclusion yields the all-arity exponential representation. Exact coefficient computations over the three labelled two-vertex Q give the claimed 4,3,2,1 bases. Four distinct nonzero coefficients prove minimal recurrence order and leading coefficients give the limiting orientation proportions. The actual standalone verifier independently enumerated all relations by transitivity and checked the DP and inclusion-exclusion 148 times plus direct and longer exact-formula cases; finite checks support, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The antichain is a canonical and maximally unconstrained finite named parameter set; its finite-stabilizer orbit profile is intrinsic to a standard homogeneous structure. The arity-two spectrum has four independent exponential scales, exact strict-order/incomparability stratification and a sharp limiting ratio; these are non-obvious and natural invariants. The general fixed-arity inclusion-exclusion mechanism gives rationality and recurrences for every r despite #P-hardness over arbitrary finite parameter posets. This supplies a reusable exact enumerative benchmark and explanation, not a renamed textbook deduction or an arbitrary finite slice.
